R8A-bear-walk-0001.name: By Paul Creek
R8A-bear-walk-0001.pressureWhy: 3.1 km on foot from the nearest parking (estimate).
R8A-bear-walk-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2010 (16 years old), 330 m E: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2023 (fire K52125), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
S facing slope, 12 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Paul Creek 110 m S: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Town of Princeton, about 43 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 49.25694, -120.09289, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 3.1 km SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 227 m, about 86 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 8-3, Region 8. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).
